description.value: The study examined whether COMT Val158Met Val allele dosage influences neurodegeneration in dopamine-innervated brain regions using whole-brain structural MRI voxel-based morphometry in healthy controls and three dementia syndromes.

spans.text: Our findings link COMT genotype to the integrity of DA-innervated regions in patients with neurodegenerative disease.

value: Increased DA catabolism might prove deleterious to DA-reliant regions
reduced synaptic DA availability might protect vulnerable tissues by reducing metabolic demand or by inducing long-term compensatory enhancement of DA-innervated regions

spans.text: Increased DA catabolism might prove deleterious to DA-reliant regions; conversely, reduced synaptic DA availability might protect vulnerable tissues by reducing metabolic demand or by inducing long-term compensatory enhancement of DA-innervated regions.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional study of healthy controls and patients with Alzheimer disease, behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, and semantic dementia who underwent COMT genotyping and structural MRI.

spans.text: We conducted a whole-brain voxel-wise structural MRI analysis on a large subject pool (n = 252, table 1, tables e-1 and e-2 on the Neurology® Web site at www.neurology.org) composed of healthy controls and 3 clinical dementia syndromes: Alzheimer disease (AD), behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), and semantic dementia (SemD).

spans.text: In a whole brain analysis across all subjects, increasing Val allele dosage was associated with decreasing gray matter intensity in only 6 regions (p < 0.001, uncorrected; extent threshold = 10 voxels; figure, A, table 2), including clusters in midline ventral midbrain in the vicinity of the VTA, ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC), bilateral dorsal midinsula/frontal operculum (dMI/FO), left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), and right ventral striatum (VStr).
First, we explored whether the COMT Val158Met Val allele exerts dose-dependent linear effects on brain structure.

A total of 252 subjects, including healthy controls and patients with Alzheimer disease, behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, and semantic dementia, underwent COMT genotyping and structural MRI.
Structural MRI scans were acquired at the San Francisco Veterans Affairs Medical Center's 1.5-T Magnetom Vision system (Siemens Inc., Iselin, NJ) using a standard quadrature head coil.

A volumetric magnetization-prepared rapid gradient echo (MPRAGE) MRI (repetition time/echo time/inversion time = 0/4/300 msec) sequence was used to obtain a T1-weighted image of the entire brain (15° flip angle, coronal orientation perpendicular to the double spin echo sequence, 1.0-mm2 in-plane resolution of 1.5-mm slab thickness).
